title: Spanish national arrested at Katunayake Airport with Rs. 110 Mn worth of Cocaine
byline: The Sri Lanka Customs Narcotics Control Unit has arrested a 79-year-old Spanish national after discovering a haul of cocaine valued at nearly Rs. 110 million hidden inside his luggage.

title: Port City Colombo attracts US $ 2.19bn in investments to date: Minister
byline: Port City Colombo has attracted investments worth US $ 2.19 billion to date, Finance Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha told Parliament yesterday.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling Nadu rice above control price
byline: A supermarket in Gampola has been fined Rs. 500,000 after pleading guilty to selling local Nadu rice above the government-controlled maximum retail price, the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) said.

title: Govt. on alert over rising crimes involving foreign nationals
byline: The government is on high alert over an increasing number of crimes involving foreign nationals across Sri Lanka, following a recent abduction and murder of a Chinese national linked to a suspected rivalry between Chinese groups in Colombo.

title: Two Sri Lankans suspected in Wattala shooting detained in India
byline: Two Sri Lankan nationals suspected of involvement in a shooting incident in Wattala have been detained by Indian Marine Police after allegedly entering India illegally by boat, according to the Hindu.

title: Two Chinese win world’s top Maths prize for solving century-old problems
byline: Two Chinese academics have won the world’s top prize for mathematics for the first time, according to state media.

title: Farewell Ambassador Qi Zhenhong of China!
byline: Sri Lanka has always been a global trading hub and as result many Envoy appointments are recorded through its long history. Among notable envoys recorded are Emperor Ashoka’s Envoys (3rd Century BC), Persian Envoys (2nd Century BC), Roman Envoys (1st Century AD), Chinese Buddhist Scholars (5th Century AD) and Chinese Admiral Zheng He (14th Century AD).

title: Five people injured after elephant attacks van
byline: Five people were injured when an elephant attacked a van travelling from Padukka to Anuradhapura yesterday.

title: I will come back to Parliament in 2029 and make sure that Minister Harshana Nanayakkara in prison: Archchuna
byline: Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara was asleep after a booze at the time of the clash in Negombo Prison, Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna alleged in Parliament yesterday.

title: Paddy cultivators stage protest in Anuradhapura
byline: Paddy cultivators in the Anuradhapura District yesterday staged a protest in Anuradhapura town against the poor guaranteed price for paddy and demanded a minimum price of Rs.150 per kilo.

title: Sri Lanka, U.S. discuss collaboration on dengue control measures
byline: Sri Lanka and the United States have discussed possible collaboration on dengue control measures as the country continues to battle a sharp surge in infections this year.

title: Calls grow for customs reforms to speed up import container clearance
byline: Sri Lanka’s import container clearance process is facing growing criticism, with industry stakeholders urging authorities to implement long-delayed customs reforms to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

title: Retirement age extension a move nothing but to please Chief Justice: Dayasiri
byline: As the government confirmed that an amendment will be introduced to extend the retirement age of judges, one opposition member said it will be made to please the current Chief Justice.

title: KKS night mail train derails
byline: The night mail train travelling from Colombo Fort to Kankesanthurai (KKS) derailed near Senarathgama Railway Station, causing disruptions to services on the Northern railway line.

title: Using unverified home dengue remedies leave patients critically ill
byline: Some dengue patients have become critically ill after using unverified home remedies, including papaya leaf juice, and have suffered various complications, the Borella National Ayurveda Hospital physician Dr. Saminda Ariyaratne said

title: ’Thank You Friends’: PM Modi’s Reel Tops 303 Million Views Amid CJP Protest
byline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has shattered digital viewing records, capturing a staggering global milestone with over 303 million views on a single Instagram reel within 24 hours.

title: Iran rescues 28 Indian seafarers after vessel attacked
byline: All 28 Indian crew members on board a Mozambique-flagged ship have been safely rescued after coming under attack near Iran’s territorial waters.

title: India’s education minister resigns after weeks of ‘Cockroach’ protests
byline: India’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned following weeks of youth protests over a series of examination paper leaks.

title: Tharoor, Mano discuss Indo-Lanka ties, regional cooperation and democratic governance
byline: Acclaimed author, parliamentarian and Chairman of India’s Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs, Dr. Shashi Tharoor MP, held a cordial and substantive meeting with Tamil Progressive Alliance Leader and Member of Parliament Mano Ganesan and TPA Vice President for International Relations Barath Arullsamy during his recent visit to Colombo.

title: CAA, STF seize expired fertilizer stock in Kaduwela raid
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA), together with the Police Special Task Force (STF), has seized a stock of expired fertilizers that had allegedly been secretly stored in lorries by an institution in the Bomiriya area of Kaduwela.

title: Sri Lanka revises guidelines for appointment of President’s Counsel
byline: Sri Lanka has revised the guidelines governing the appointment of President’s Counsel, introducing a minimum 20-year professional experience requirement for eligible Attorneys-at-Law.

title: At least 35 killed in Syria bus collision, health ministry says
byline: Thirty-five people were killed and 30 injured in a collision between two passenger buses on Syria’s Deir al-Zor-Damascus road, a health ministry official tells state news agency SANA.

title: Houthis fire on Saudi Red Sea oil sites
byline: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi militants fired on Saudi ​oil installations in two ports on the Red Sea coast on Saturday and Saudi-backed forces bombed the Houthis, as the war in the Gulf that ‌has disrupted global supplies extended to a second front.

title: Cassilingham receives appointment as SLPP Jaffna District Organizer
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Politburo Member G. Cassilingham today officially received his letter of appointment as the party’s Jaffna District Organizer from SLPP National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa at the party headquarters on Nelum Mawatha in Colombo.

title: Cockroach Janta Party calls off protest after Indian govt meets demands
byline: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) today (25 July) withdrew its protest against exam paper leaks after the Indian government accepted all its demands, following 36 days of demonstrations.

title: Jaffna Kings franchise agreement terminated over alleged integrity breaches
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has announced that the Jaffna Kings franchise agreement in the Lanka Premier League (LPL) has been terminated following alleged breaches of anti-corruption and integrity provisions.

title: Nine arrested after attack on Wildlife and STF officers in Kilinochchi
byline: A group of individuals has been arrested for obstructing the duties of Wildlife and Police Special Task Force (STF) personnel and launching an attack on them during a raid in Akkarayankulam, Kilinochchi.

title: Former Sri Lanka Cricket President Upali Dharmadasa passes away
byline: ​Former Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) President Upali Dharmadasa has passed away at the age of 72.

title: Update - Restaurant owner dies following Bellanwila shooting
byline: A local restaurant owner (55) who was critically injured in a shooting incident in the Bellanwila area earlier today has succumbed to his injuries, Police said.

title: Were outsiders being accommodated at Presidential Residences?
byline: The President’s Media Division (PMD) has responded to reports alleging that outsiders were being accommodated at Presidential Residences.

title: Pralhad Joshi appointed Union Education Minister
byline: Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new Union Education Minister on Saturday (July 25, 2026) after the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhanfollowing nationwide protests.

title: At least 35 killed in Syria bus collision, health ministry says
byline: Thirty-five people were killed and 30 injured in a collision between two passenger buses on Syria’s Deir al-Zor-Damascus road, a health ministry official tells state news agency SANA.
